reason: The pressure patch kit is the obvious first choice for the punctured habitat wall.
expectation: The kit should seal the puncture so the habitat can be refilled.

effect: The patch stopped the leak, so refilling the habitat is the next apparent step.
reaction: The backing plate makes the repair feel physically plausible.
reason: The breathing-gas supply is the obvious means of refilling the sealed habitat.
expectation: The supply should refill the habitat now that its wall is sealed.

effect: The habitat is breathable, and the new goal is to stabilize the damaged landing support.
reaction: The regulator and gauge make the refill feel grounded.
reason: Shipping braces look suitable for supporting the damaged landing leg, though I am not sure whether the service tool is also needed.
expectation: The braces should help stabilize the damaged support.

alternatives.reason: I could check its available partners first.

effect: The braces cannot be used directly on the support; their listed partner is the service tool.
reaction: The failed attempt clarifies that the braces need preparation.
reason: The compatibility list identifies the service tool as the next step for the braces.
expectation: The tool should prepare the braces for stabilizing the landing support.

effect: The service tool converted the shipping braces into usable steel lengths and sheet.
reaction: Cutting the bracing free makes the preparation clear.
reason: The prepared steel may now be usable to stabilize the low landing support.
expectation: The steel should reinforce the damaged support, possibly with the service tool.

effect: The steel formed a load-spreading crib, stabilizing the landing support and completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: The explanation of the crib and inspection points made the repair feel satisfyingly grounded.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the crib was most worthwhile: it resolved the landing damage and explained how the frame spreads the load without pretending to be a permanent replacement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the braces directly on the support was the least worthwhile decision, though its compatibility feedback identified the needed preparation.

surprise.text: The braces first became general-purpose steel rather than a ready-made support; the resulting crib was a more considered repair than I expected.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary. The initial incompatibility was clarified when the tool cut the braces free of their shipping joints.

continue.text: Yes. The practical repair details and the promise of further discovery would make me curious to see how the expedition develops.
